name_note: Papers state that Anaerobutyricum soehngenii was previously called Eubacterium hallii; the NCBI organism name of the GTDB representative genome is Anaerobutyricum hallii, the other species of the same genus.

sentences.text: Anaerobutyricum soehngenii belongs to the genus Anaerobutyricum, which is prevalent in the human gut microbiota and produces short-chain fatty acids that influence host metabolism and inflammation.
A genomic analysis of 84 Anaerobutyricum genomes reported that Anaerobutyricum hallii and Anaerobutyricum soehngenii are specific to human hosts, with longer genomes and lower GC content.
Anaerobutyricum soehngenii, previously called Eubacterium hallii, is described as a butyrate-producing next-generation beneficial microbe generally recognized as safe.

In a 3-month double-blind randomized placebo-controlled intervention in 98 prediabetic insulin-resistant adults, treated subjects showed significantly reduced glycemic variability and improved glycemic control.
Several short-term intervention trials with strain L2-7 were reported to show improvement of insulin sensitivity in prediabetic subjects and type 2 diabetes patients.
